page: UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is a general-purpose virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor running at 2.0 GHz, with 4 physical cores and a 1-to-1 thread-to-core ratio. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes 150 GB of local SSD storage alongside one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark data shows top-tier single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 3812.16 and a Geekbench single-core score of 2234.0. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression (40.86 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (16.93 GB/sec) also rank in the top tier. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth fall into the average tier, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 7140.0 and a Passmark memory score ranking in the bottom 25%.

The server supports advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI. The shared CPU allocation presents a potential tradeoff for sustained multi-threaded workloads, as reflected in the average multi-core benchmark results. This server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, text processing, and light web serving, but is less optimal for memory-intensive operations or large-scale LLM inference.
description: The UpCloud PREMIUM-4xCPU-16GB is an x86_64 general-purpose virtual server running on the KVM hypervisor. It features 4 shared vCPUs from an AMD EPYC 9575F processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM and 150 GB of local SSD storage. While its multi-core and memory bandwidth benchmarks sit in the average tier, the server delivers top-tier single-core performance, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core score of 2234.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. The server includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration via SHA-NI and AES. It also provides one complimentary public IPv4 address. This hardware profile makes it highly suitable for general-purpose applications, text processing, and lightweight web serving, though the shared CPU allocation and weaker memory performance present tradeoffs for sustained multi-threaded or memory-heavy workloads.
